label: Narrative A
title: A bridge the community depends on
paragraph: Picture a flood-damaged bridge on a federal road that school buses and ambulances use. In this hypothetical example, Congress provides $10 million for the agency’s bridge-repair program. OMB apportions $2.5 million for the period, and the agency allots $1 million to the district responsible for that road. The district signs a $750,000 repair contract, creating an obligation. After engineers accept the first stage of work, an authorized $500,000 payment is issued through Treasury. The remaining $250,000 is an unpaid obligation. A reviewer can follow the payment back through the contract, allotment, apportionment, and original appropriation.

label: Narrative B
title: Safe drinking water at a federal site
paragraph: A failing treatment system has closed part of a federal recreation site. Congress provides a hypothetical $10 million for the agency’s water-system repairs. OMB apportions $2.5 million, and the agency allots $1 million to the field office overseeing the site. The field office awards a $750,000 contract to replace the treatment equipment, recording an obligation for that amount. Once equipment has been delivered and the first installation milestone accepted, the agency authorizes a $500,000 payment through Treasury. The remaining contract balance is $250,000. The record connects a useful outcome—safe water and a reopened site—to the funding decisions and accepted work behind the payment.

label: Narrative C
title: Keeping a clinic open
paragraph: A federal clinic needs a failed ventilation system replaced so patient rooms can stay in service. A hypothetical $10 million appropriation supports the agency’s facility-repair program. OMB apportions $2.5 million for the period; the agency allots $1 million to the region managing the clinic. A signed $750,000 installation contract creates the obligation. After the first wing is completed and inspected, an approved $500,000 invoice is paid through Treasury, leaving $250,000 of the obligation unpaid. Verification asks whether the payment matches accepted work, the contract was properly approved, and the obligation stayed within the available allotment.
